questions.q: Which description of Wilkinson's catalyst is correct?
options: RhCl(PPh₃)₃, a 16-electron, roughly square planar Rh(I) complex
A solid Rh metal surface poisoned with PPh₃
questions.explain: Wilkinson's catalyst is RhCl(PPh₃)₃ with one chloride and rhodium in the +1 (d⁸) state; it is a 16-electron, nearly square planar, homogeneous catalyst. Writing it as [Rh(PPh₃)₃]Cl₃ is the classic trap.

questions.q: CH₂=CH–CH₂–CHO is treated with H₂ in the presence of RhCl(PPh₃)₃ in benzene at 25 °C. The main product is
questions.explain: Wilkinson's catalyst reduces the unhindered terminal C=C but leaves the C=O group alone, so only the alkene is hydrogenated.

questions.q: Which alkene is hydrogenated most slowly (or not at all) with H₂ / RhCl(PPh₃)₃?
questions.explain: 2,3-Dimethylbut-2-ene is a tetrasubstituted alkene, too crowded to bind the bulky rhodium centre; Wilkinson's catalyst works well only on mono- and disubstituted C=C bonds.

questions.q: In the catalytic cycle of Wilkinson's catalyst, which step changes rhodium from +1 to +3?
options: Migratory insertion of the alkene into Rh–H
questions.explain: Oxidative addition of H₂ gives a Rh(III) dihydride; reductive elimination later releases the alkane and regenerates Rh(I). Ligand loss and insertion do not change the oxidation state in this way.
